cards.title: Unit Testing Basics
cards.content:
Jasmine & Karma

Angular uses Jasmine as the testing framework (providing describe, it, expect) and Karma as the test runner (executing tests in a real browser).

Newer Angular versions also support Jest as an alternative test runner for faster, headless testing.

cards.title: The Angular TestBed
cards.content:
TestBed Configuration

TestBed is the primary API for writing Angular unit tests. It creates an Angular testing module, allowing you to configure components, services, and dependencies.

await TestBed.configureTestingModule({
  imports: [MyComponent],
  providers: [MyService]
}).compileComponents();

cards.title: Mocking Dependencies
cards.content:
Isolating Tests

To unit test effectively, you should isolate the component or service by mocking its dependencies. You can provide mock objects or use Jasmine spies (jasmine.createSpyObj).

const mockAuth = { isLoggedIn: () => true };
TestBed.configureTestingModule({
  providers: [{ provide: AuthService, useValue: mockAuth }]
});
